scope: Theorem 8.2 (Finite-component exterior equality rigidity) of the manuscript “Equality and rigidity in the spacetime Penrose inequality” (preprints/Equality-and-rigidity-in-the-spacetime-Penrose-inequality-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4f1aab59ba484eb8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 78-79. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: Let (M, g, K) be a smooth connected orientable complete initial data set without boundary, consisting of a compact core and finitely many asymptotically flat ends. On each end assume g − δ = O2(r−q), K = O1(r−1−q), with 78 q > 1/2, and existing finite ADM flux limits. Assume that µ and |J|g are integrable and that µ ≥ |J|g everywhere. Choose an end and a finite nonempty disjoint union S = ℓ ⨆︂ i=1 Si, 1 ≤ ℓ < ∞, of compact connected smooth embedded two-sided surfaces without boundary, separating that end from a complementary region. Let Mext be the closure of the connected side toward the chosen end. Suppose that ∂Mext = S, that Mext has exactly this one end, and that, for the normal pointing into Mext: (i) every Si is a future MOTS, so HSi + trSi K = 0; (ii) S is outermost in the partial-coincidence sense of Definition 8.1; (iii) every enclosing cut in the closed exterior has area at least A = |S|g = ∑︁ℓ i=1 |Si|g > 0. Let (E, P) be the ADM vector of the chosen end. If E > |P|δ, m = √︂ E2 − |P|2 δ = √︄ A 16π , (8.1) then ℓ = 1 and S is diffeomorphic to a sphere. There is a proper smooth spacelike embedding of the entire original Mext into the maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime of mass m, inducing g and the given K for a consistent future unit normal. The chosen end approaches the corresponding spatial infinity. The image of S is a smooth cross-section of the corresponding future horizon or the bifurcation sphere. The embedding and its future normal are smooth up to S, and the image extends as a smooth spacelike hypersurface through that boundary.
